model.name: Decision / Rationale
model.purpose: Govern the decision as an inspectable knowledge object: the issue to be resolved, the objectives and constraints that frame it, the alternatives considered, the criteria and evaluation applied, the selected outcome and its disposition, together with the rationale, evidence citations, authority, lifecycle, provenance and access governance that let a machine agent understand, reconstruct and reuse the choice.
model.scope_statement: WM-KNW-010 governs the content of a decision taken on a specific occasion and the reasoning offered for it, independently of storage format and access interface. It covers stable decision identity and version discrimination; decision type and jurisdictional profile; the decision question, objectives, context and affected subjects; constraints and the decision rules relied upon; the candidate alternative set including any required no-action baseline; eligibility screening and recorded exclusion; criteria, measures, scales and weights; evaluation results, comparison and sensitivity; the selected alternative, disposition, explicit outcome statement, attached conditions and stated consequences; the rationale and argument structure that justify the outcome together with citations to evidence; the participants, roles and authority basis under which the decision was taken; and the lifecycle, provenance, access, retention and quality governance of decision content. It does not govern the activity that produced the decision, the document that carries it, the legal instrument that may enact it, the evidence items it cites, any executable rule or decision service, or downstream implementation.
in_scope: Stable decision identity, version discriminator and supersession links between decisions
Decision type, jurisdictional profile binding and profile-required content elements
The decision question, its admissible answer space and the problem or issue that triggered it
Objectives, critical success factors and expected effects on declared indicators
Decision context, dependencies on input data and upstream decisions, and affected subjects
Binding constraints, admissibility conditions and the decision rules relied upon, stated declaratively
The registered candidate alternative set, including a no-action or business-as-usual baseline where a profile requires one
Eligibility screening and recorded reasons for excluding alternatives from detailed evaluation
Evaluation criteria, measures, scales, preference directions and weighting schemes
Recorded evaluation results, aggregation, ranking and sensitivity findings
The selected alternative, disposition, explicit outcome statement, effect onset and applicability
Conditions, reservations, accepted risks, stated consequences and follow-on decisions
Rationale, argument structure and explanation linking the outcome to objectives, criteria and cited evidence
Participants, roles, delegation and the authority basis on which the decision was taken
Decision-content lifecycle states, revision history, provenance, access classification, retention and quality governance
out_of_scope: The decision-making or approval activity itself, including convening, deliberation, voting and approval execution (WM-ACT-024)
The document or record container that renders, files, publishes or preserves the decision (WM-REC-010)
The legal judgment as a binding legal instrument, its enforceability and its citation regime (WM-POL-021)
Generic claim assertion, truth-value and claim-conflict machinery (WM-KNW-007)
Evidence items themselves, their appraisal, integrity and chain of custody (WM-KNW-008)
Executable rules, policies, decision services and rule engines, and their runtime evaluation or enforcement
Audit-trail records produced by an external audit or logging service
Implementation, delivery and change execution that follows a decision (WM-ACT-032)
Domain-specific decision rule content such as clinical protocols, credit scorecards, procurement award formulas or sentencing guidelines
Mathematical decision-analysis method definitions such as utility theory, AHP, ELECTRE or PROMETHEE, which bind only as optional external methods

boundary_notes.distinction: This model governs decision content. DMN's Decision element only points at decisionMaker, decisionOwner, usingProcess and usingTask by reference, and ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 places decision management as a process. Convening, deliberation, voting and approval execution therefore belong to the activity model and are referenced, never reproduced here.

Akoma Ntoso separates the abstract Work and its Expression from the Manifestation and Item that carry it. Decision content is the governed subject here; rendering, filing, formatting, publication and preservation of the carrying record belong to the record model.

A judgment is a legal instrument with binding force, its own citation regime and a judgmentBody whose introduction, background, motivation and decision sections are editorially structured. This model captures the decision content a judgment may express, not the instrument's legal effect.

A claim asserts that something is the case. A decision selects among registered alternatives and produces a disposition. Generic assertion identity, truth-value and claim-conflict machinery stay with the parent model; only decision-specific specialisation is modelled here.

Cited evidence is bound by identifier with a stated role in an evaluation result. Evidence appraisal, integrity, sufficiency and chain of custody remain with the evidence model; NASA's guidance on assumptions and their supporting evidence is used only to justify the citation binding.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Executable rule, policy or decision service
boundary_notes.distinction: DMN decision logic, business knowledge models and decision tables are executable artefacts deployed and run by a decision service. This model records the rules relied upon, their declared hit policy and a versioned reference to the source rule, and never owns runtime evaluation, enforcement or the engine's execution trace.

A change request may be resolved by a decision; the decision carries a back-reference to the resolved issue. The request's own lifecycle, prioritisation and the implementation of the change belong to that model, as does the monitoring and compliance work that a record of decision may direct.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-KNW-010 rationale, participation and governance areas (same model)
boundary_notes.distinction: Argument structure, explanation, participants and authority basis, and the lifecycle, provenance, access, retention and audit governance of decision content are governed by the other areas of this same model. The decision-core structures supply their subject matter by reference and do not restate them.

bundle.name: Decision framing and identity
bundle.description: How a specific decision is identified, typed against a jurisdictional profile, and framed by its question, objectives, context, constraints and the rules it relies upon.

layer.name: Decision identity and classification
layer.description: Stable identification of the decision content, discrimination between its expressions, and its classification against a decision type and jurisdictional profile.

finding.name: Decision identity and version discriminator
finding.description: How one governed decision is stably identified, how successive expressions of the same decision are discriminated, how the identity of the decision content is kept distinct from the identity of the record that carries it, and how supersession and alternate jurisdictional identifiers are recorded.

questions.text: Which authoritative master-system identifier designates this decision, and which registry mints and resolves it?
answer_data: Issuing system of record and identifier scheme name

questions.text: What version discriminator distinguishes this expression of the decision from earlier or later expressions of the same decision?
answer_data: Rule by which the discriminator increases
Reference to the immediately preceding expression

questions.text: Is the identifier scoped to the decision content itself or to the record that carries it, and how is that distinction represented?
answer_data: Carrying-record reference and its own identifier
Statement of which identifier is authoritative for citation

questions.text: Which prior decision, if any, does this decision supersede, amend, reaffirm or reverse, and by which identifier?
answer_data: Scope of the supersession, whole or partial

questions.text: Which external or jurisdictional identifiers are carried as labelled alternate identifiers for this decision?
answer_data: Statement that the alternate identifier is non-authoritative

data_elements.name: Decision identifier
data_elements.description: The authoritative identifier of the governed decision content, minted according to the identity priority order.

data_elements.name: Version discriminator
data_elements.description: Label or ordinal distinguishing this expression of the decision content from other expressions of the same decision; never a bare date.

data_elements.name: Carrying record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the document or record container in which this decision content is expressed, held for navigation only.

data_elements.name: Supersedes reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of a prior decision that this decision supersedes, amends, reaffirms or reverses, with the relation code.

data_elements.name: Alternate identifier
data_elements.description: Labelled non-authoritative identifier from an external scheme, such as a case, docket or published-citation reference.

finding.inline_only_rationale: Identity is reference data carried directly on the decision record: identifier values, a version discriminator, typed links to superseded decisions and labelled alternate identifiers. No separate governed artefact is produced, and any rendered identifier block belongs to the carrying record model rather than to decision content.

bundle.name: Decision framing and identity
bundle.description: How a specific decision is identified, typed against a jurisdictional profile, and framed by its question, objectives, context, constraints and the rules it relies upon.

layer.name: Decision question, objectives and context
layer.description: What the decision is being asked to settle, what it is intended to achieve, and the context, dependencies and affected subjects within which it is taken.

finding.name: Decision question, triggering issue and admissible answer space
finding.description: The single question the decision answers, the admissible answers to that question, the problem or issue that made the decision necessary, and whether the question decomposes into required sub-decisions.

questions.text: What single question does this decision answer, stated so that a recorded answer can be checked against it?
answer_data: Natural language and locale of the statement
Test for whether a candidate answer responds to the question

questions.text: What is the admissible answer space for that question, and is it an enumerated set or an open expression?
answer_data: Whether the space is closed or open
Datatype or unit of an admissible answer

questions.text: What problem, need or issue made this decision necessary, and which upstream item raised it?
answer_data: Rationale for intervention, such as a stated market failure or equity concern

questions.text: Is this an atomic decision, or does it decompose into sub-decisions that must be settled for the answer to hold?

data_elements.name: Decision question
data_elements.description: The question the decision answers, expressed as a single interrogative statement.

data_elements.name: Admissible answer space
data_elements.description: Statement or enumeration of the answers admissible for the decision question.

data_elements.name: Problem statement
data_elements.description: The need, issue or case for change that makes the decision necessary.

data_elements.name: Triggering issue reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the change request, incident or request that the decision is taken to resolve.

data_elements.name: Sub-decision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a decision whose outcome this decision requires.

finding.inline_only_rationale: The question, its admissible answers and the problem statement are short authored text fields plus typed references. DMN carries them as simple string children of the Decision element, and holding them inline keeps the answer directly comparable with the recorded outcome statement without a separate artefact to keep in step.

bundle.name: Alternatives, screening and evaluation
bundle.description: The candidate alternatives placed under consideration including any required baseline, the screening that determines eligibility, the criteria and weights used for comparison, and the recorded evaluation results.

layer.name: Candidate alternatives and eligibility
layer.description: Registration of the alternatives under consideration, including any profile-required baseline, and the screening that admits or excludes each from detailed evaluation.

finding.name: Candidate alternative set and mandatory baseline
finding.description: The alternatives placed under consideration, how each is identified and described, whether a no-action or business-as-usual baseline is present as the profile requires, and how variants of one alternative are distinguished from genuinely distinct alternatives.

questions.text: Which candidate alternatives were placed under consideration, and how is each identified within this decision?
answer_data: Stage at which it entered consideration, longlist or shortlist

questions.text: Is a no-action, business-as-usual or do-minimum baseline included, and if not, on what stated basis is it absent?
answer_data: Baseline kind, no action, business as usual or do minimum
Recorded justification where the bound profile allows its absence

questions.text: How are variants of the same alternative distinguished from genuinely distinct alternatives?
answer_data: Variant relation to a parent alternative
Dimension on which the variant differs, such as scope, solution, delivery, implementation or funding
Whether the variant is scored independently

questions.text: What does each alternative commit to doing, described in terms sufficient for it to be evaluated against the declared criteria?
answer_data: Distinguishing features relative to the baseline

data_elements.name: Alternative
data_elements.description: A registered candidate alternative with its identifier, name, description and registration ordinal.

data_elements.name: Alternative kind code
data_elements.description: Code marking an alternative as the baseline, a do-minimum, a preferred way forward, a more ambitious or less ambitious variant, or an ordinary candidate.

data_elements.name: Baseline alternative reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the alternative that serves as the no-action or business-as-usual benchmark for comparison.

data_elements.name: Variant-of reference
data_elements.description: Reference from a variant to the alternative it varies, with the dimension of variation.

finding.inline_only_rationale: Alternatives are append-only structured records held on the decision: an identifier, a kind code, a description and a variant link. They must stay directly addressable from evaluation results and from the outcome, so extracting them into a separate artefact would add an indirection with no governance benefit.

bundle.name: Alternatives, screening and evaluation
bundle.description: The candidate alternatives placed under consideration including any required baseline, the screening that determines eligibility, the criteria and weights used for comparison, and the recorded evaluation results.

layer.name: Criteria and evaluation results
layer.description: The declared basis for comparing alternatives and the recorded results of applying it, including aggregation, ranking and sensitivity.

finding.name: Evaluation results, comparison and sensitivity
finding.description: The recorded result of each alternative against each criterion for one evaluation round, any aggregation and ranking derived from those results, the sensitivity of the ranking to changed scores, weights or assumptions, the evidence cited by reference in support of results, and the status of contested or provisional results.

questions.text: What result does each alternative achieve on each declared criterion, in the criterion's own measure?
answer_data: Result value per alternative and criterion
Whether the result is measured, estimated or asserted

questions.text: What ranking or comparison follows from the recorded results, and by which aggregation was it derived?
answer_data: Aggregation rule applied, including any monetised summary measure

questions.text: How sensitive is the ranking to plausible changes in scores, weights or declared assumptions?
answer_data: Sensitivity test description and the parameter varied
Range over which the ranking is stable
Any assumption whose failure reverses the ranking

questions.text: Which evidence items are cited in support of each recorded result, and what role does each citation play?
answer_data: Role of the citation, such as supporting a score or an assumption
Statement that appraisal of the evidence stays with the evidence model

questions.text: Which recorded results are contested, provisional or adjusted for known bias?
answer_data: Nature of the contest or provisional condition
Bias adjustment applied and its basis

data_elements.name: Evaluation round
data_elements.description: An append-only round of evaluation, identified by a monotonically increasing ordinal, containing results for the alternatives evaluated in it.

data_elements.name: Criterion result
data_elements.description: The result achieved by one alternative on one criterion within a round.

data_elements.name: Aggregate result
data_elements.description: Aggregated value for an alternative derived from its criterion results under the declared aggregation rule.

data_elements.name: Ranking position
data_elements.description: Position of an alternative in the ordering produced by the round.

data_elements.name: Sensitivity finding
data_elements.description: Statement of how the ranking responds to a varied score, weight or assumption.

data_elements.name: Cited evidence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an evidence item cited in support of a result or assumption, with the role of the citation.

data_elements.name: Result status code
data_elements.description: Status marking a result as settled, provisional, contested or bias-adjusted.

artifacts.name: Alternative-by-criterion comparison matrix
artifacts.description: Matrix recording each admitted alternative's result against each declared criterion for one evaluation round, with aggregation, ranking, sensitivity annotations and citation slots referencing evidence by identifier. It is a governed record of what the comparison showed; it does not execute the comparison and does not carry evidence content.
media_or_form: tabular matrix with alternatives and criteria as axes
artifacts.identity_strategy: Decision master identifier plus a zero-padded, monotonically increasing evaluation-round ordinal; the ordinal is a sequence number and never encodes a date. Superseded rounds keep their ordinal and remain resolvable.

bundle.name: Selection, disposition and stated consequences
bundle.description: The alternative selected, the disposition and explicit outcome statement that answers the decision question, and the conditions, reservations and consequences the decision states as part of its own content.

layer.name: Decision outcome and attached conditions
layer.description: The explicit answer to the decision question with its disposition and applicability, and the conditions, unresolved matters and consequences stated as part of the decision.

finding.name: Selected alternative, disposition and outcome statement
finding.description: Which alternative is selected, the disposition the decision reaches, the explicit outcome statement that answers the decision question, the declared onset and applicability of effect, the factors expressly balanced, and any explained divergence from the evaluation ranking.

questions.text: Which alternative is selected, and is the disposition an approval, refusal, deferral, partial approval or a declared variant of a registered alternative?
answer_data: Description of the variant where the selection is not a registered alternative verbatim

questions.text: What is the explicit outcome statement, phrased as a direct answer to the recorded decision question?
answer_data: Check that the statement falls within the admissible answer space
Language and locale of the statement

questions.text: From when does the decision take effect, and for how long or until what event does it apply?
answer_data: Effect onset instant in RFC 3339 with seconds and offset
Applicability end instant or terminating event
Whether effect is immediate, deferred or conditional on an act by another party

questions.text: Which factors were expressly balanced in reaching this selection, including any consideration of overriding policy?
answer_data: Weight or priority the factor was given in the balance
Reference to the policy consideration where one was decisive

questions.text: How does the selection relate to the ranking produced by the evaluation, and is any divergence explained or a preferable alternative named separately?
answer_data: Ranking position of the selected alternative
Divergence explanation where the top-ranked alternative was not selected
Separately identified preferable alternative where the profile requires one

data_elements.name: Selected alternative reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the registered alternative the decision selects, or to the alternative from which the selected variant derives.

data_elements.name: Disposition code
data_elements.description: Controlled code naming the disposition reached, such as approved, refused, deferred, partially approved or withdrawn from consideration.

data_elements.name: Outcome statement
data_elements.description: Explicit statement of the decision, phrased as the answer to the recorded decision question.

data_elements.name: Effect onset
data_elements.description: Instant from which the decision takes effect, recorded in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Applicability end
data_elements.description: Instant or terminating event at which the decision ceases to apply.

data_elements.name: Balanced factor
data_elements.description: A factor or policy consideration expressly balanced in reaching the selection.

data_elements.name: Divergence explanation
data_elements.description: Recorded explanation where the selected alternative is not the one the evaluation ranked highest.

data_elements.name: Preferable alternative reference
data_elements.description: Separately identified alternative named as preferable on a stated dimension, where the bound profile requires such identification.

finding.inline_only_rationale: The outcome is a small, immutable set of fields on the decision itself: a selected-alternative reference, a disposition code, the statement answering the question and the declared effect times. The published record of decision that renders these fields is a document governed by the record model, and the approval that authorised them is an activity governed elsewhere, so producing an artefact here would claim ownership of one or both.

bundle.name: Stated reasons and argument structure
bundle.description: The reasons offered for a decision and the argument that connects premises, inference schemes and conclusions to the recorded outcome, including contrastive reasons for not selecting alternatives and any explicitly asserted causal or counterfactual reasoning.

layer.name: Stated reasons and rejection reasons
layer.description: The rationale statement issued with a decision, the discrete reason records that compose it, and the contrastive reasons recorded for alternatives that were not selected.

finding.name: Rationale statement and constituent reasons
finding.description: The holistic statement of reasons issued with a decision together with the discrete, independently citable reason records that compose it. Each reason carries its type, its polarity relative to the recorded outcome, an optional asserted weight on a named scale, and the party asserting it. The statement explains the decision; it does not restate the decision problem, option set or criteria, which the `core` split owns.

questions.text: What distinguishes the rationale statement issued with a decision from the individual reason records that compose it?
answer_data: rationale summary text with language tag
ordered list of constituent reason record identifiers
scope note stating what the summary does and does not cover

questions.text: How is each reason identified so that it can be cited independently of the decision narrative?
answer_data: master-system identifier of the decision the reason explains

questions.text: What type does each reason carry, and does it argue for or against the recorded outcome?
answer_data: reference to the governing reason taxonomy
polarity value: supporting, opposing or qualifying

questions.text: What relative weight or priority is asserted for a reason, and on which named scale is it expressed?
answer_data: scale identifier and its published definition
note on whether the weight was elicited, derived or unstated

questions.text: Which party asserted the reason, and on what stated basis of authority?
answer_data: reference to the authority basis or mandate cited

data_elements.name: Rationale summary
data_elements.description: Narrative statement of the reasons on which the decision is based, as issued with the decision.

data_elements.name: Reason statement
data_elements.description: A single discrete reason offered for or against the recorded outcome, individually identified and citable.

data_elements.name: Reason polarity
data_elements.description: Whether the reason supports, opposes or merely qualifies the recorded outcome.

data_elements.name: Asserted reason weight
data_elements.description: Relative weight or priority asserted for the reason, meaningful only with its scale reference.

data_elements.name: Asserting party reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party that asserted the reason; the party's role assignment is governed elsewhere.

artifacts.name: Statement of reasons
artifacts.description: The issued statement of reasons for a decision, generated from the canonical reason record set and carrying the rationale revision it renders.
media_or_form: rendered section of a decision notice
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derived from the authoritative master-system identifier of the decision plus a stable rationale-part key; the issue date is metadata and is never used as the identifier.

bundle.name: Stated reasons and argument structure
bundle.description: The reasons offered for a decision and the argument that connects premises, inference schemes and conclusions to the recorded outcome, including contrastive reasons for not selecting alternatives and any explicitly asserted causal or counterfactual reasoning.

layer.name: Argument structure and inference
layer.description: How premises, conclusions, inference-scheme references, critical questions and asserted conflict relations are represented, and how explicitly asserted causal or counterfactual reasoning is recorded without being upgraded beyond what was stated.

finding.name: Premises, conclusions and inference-scheme references
finding.description: The argument connecting reasons to the recorded outcome, represented with the inference itself as a first-class element rather than as an implicit edge. Covers the role each element plays (premise, conclusion, context, exception), the inference scheme referenced for each step, recorded critical questions and their responses, the support status of each premise, and asserted conflict relations. The model records asserted inference only and performs no validity or entailment evaluation.

questions.text: How are premises and conclusions distinguished within a recorded argument, and how is the inference between them represented as a first-class element?
answer_data: argument element role code per node
identifier of the inference element linking premises to conclusion
reference to any reasoning description attached to the inference

questions.text: Which inference scheme is referenced for each inference step, and where is that scheme catalogue governed?
answer_data: reference to the governing scheme catalogue and its version
flag for schemes stated informally with no catalogue entry

questions.text: Which critical questions or exceptions attached to the referenced scheme are recorded, and are they answered?
answer_data: critical question identifier from the scheme
recorded response text or explicit unanswered marker
reference to evidence or claim cited in the response

questions.text: How are asserted support relations distinguished from asserted conflict relations between argument elements?
answer_data: relation type code distinguishing support from conflict
note on any asserted preference between conflicting elements

questions.text: Is a given premise recorded as assumed, as axiomatic, or as still requiring support?
answer_data: reference to supporting claim or evidence binding where support exists
note recording that this status annotates the premise, not the decision

data_elements.name: Argument element role
data_elements.description: Role an element plays in one argument: premise, conclusion, context, exception or reasoning description.

data_elements.name: Inference scheme reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the scheme, in a governed catalogue where one exists, that the asserted inference instantiates.

data_elements.name: Critical question response
data_elements.description: Recorded response to a critical question or exception attached to the referenced scheme, or an explicit unanswered marker.

data_elements.name: Premise support status
data_elements.description: Whether a premise is assumed, axiomatic or still to be supported.

data_elements.name: Conflict assertion reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an asserted conflict or attack relation between two argument elements, with any asserted preference between them.

artifacts.name: Argument structure export
artifacts.description: A projection of the canonical argument record set as a node-and-link structure suitable for exchange with argumentation or assurance-case tooling.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derived from the decision's master-system identifier plus the argument key; where the export is exchanged externally it additionally carries the governed scheme-catalogue IRIs it references.

bundle.name: Grounding, appraisal and epistemic qualification
bundle.description: How rationale elements bind to governed claims and evidence, how the decision authority's own appraisal of that evidence is recorded separately from the evidence body's certainty grade, and how assumptions, dependencies, uncertainty, trade-offs, sensitivity and contestation are qualified.

layer.name: Claim and evidence bindings
layer.description: Reference bindings from rationale elements to governed claims in WM-KNW-007 and governed evidence in WM-KNW-008, carrying the role, citation type, locator and stance but never a copy of the referenced content.

finding.name: Claim references used as premises and conclusions
finding.description: Bindings that place a governed claim into an argument role, pin the claim version relied on when the reasoning was asserted, and mark any local paraphrase as a restatement. Claim identity, wording, revision and verification status remain in WM-KNW-007; this finding owns only the binding and the role the claim plays in one argument.

questions.text: Which governed claim does each premise or conclusion slot reference, and by which identifier?
answer_data: identifier scheme used for the reference
resolution status of the reference at binding time

questions.text: What role does a referenced claim play in this argument: premise, conclusion, context or exception?
answer_data: claim role code within the argument
identifier of the argument element occupying that role
note where one claim occupies multiple roles across arguments

questions.text: How is a locally paraphrased restatement of a claim distinguished from the governed claim it references?
answer_data: local restatement text with an explicit restatement marker
referenced claim identifier the restatement stands for
flag indicating whether the restatement was reviewed against the source claim

questions.text: How does this record express which claim version the reasoning relied on, given that claim revision is governed elsewhere?
answer_data: pinned claim version or revision identifier
note describing how a later claim revision is reported rather than silently followed

data_elements.name: Claim reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a governed claim in WM-KNW-007 used as a premise, conclusion, context or exception.

data_elements.name: Claim role in argument
data_elements.description: Role the referenced claim occupies within this argument.

data_elements.name: Claim version pin
data_elements.description: Version or revision of the referenced claim that the reasoning relied on at the time it was asserted.

data_elements.name: Local claim restatement
data_elements.description: Paraphrase of a referenced claim recorded for readability, explicitly marked as a restatement and never authoritative.

finding.inline_only_rationale: A claim binding is pure reference data: an identifier, a version pin, a role code and an optional marked paraphrase. Giving it an artefact would produce a second store of claim text outside WM-KNW-007 and create exactly the duplication the reference relation exists to prevent, since a materialised binding document would age independently of the governed claim. The binding therefore lives inline on the argument element and is projected only inside the argument structure export owned by the argument-structure finding.

bundle.name: Grounding, appraisal and epistemic qualification
bundle.description: How rationale elements bind to governed claims and evidence, how the decision authority's own appraisal of that evidence is recorded separately from the evidence body's certainty grade, and how assumptions, dependencies, uncertainty, trade-offs, sensitivity and contestation are qualified.

layer.name: Claim and evidence bindings
layer.description: Reference bindings from rationale elements to governed claims in WM-KNW-007 and governed evidence in WM-KNW-008, carrying the role, citation type, locator and stance but never a copy of the referenced content.

finding.name: Evidence citation bindings
finding.description: Bindings from a reason or premise to a governed evidence item in WM-KNW-008, carrying the citation type drawn from a governed vocabulary, a locator pinpointing the relevant part of the cited resource, the stance of the citation, and whether the citation was made by the decision author or inherited from an intermediate source. Evidence content, acquisition, custody and grading remain in WM-KNW-008.

questions.text: Which governed evidence item does a citation bind to, and how is an unresolvable reference recorded?
answer_data: gap record where the reference does not resolve

questions.text: What is the type of the citation act: cited as evidence, cited as authority, cited as quoted, disagreed with or refuted?
answer_data: citation type code drawn from a governed citation vocabulary
free-text note where no vocabulary term fits

questions.text: How is the specific part of the cited resource pinpointed rather than the resource being cited as a whole?
answer_data: locator object with selector kind and parameters
exact quotation with prefix and suffix context where text is cited
position range or media fragment where applicable

questions.text: Does the citation support the reason it is attached to, counter it, or supply context only?
answer_data: identifier of the reason or premise the citation attaches to
note where the same evidence is cited on both sides

questions.text: Was the citation asserted by the decision author, or inherited from an intermediate document that cited the source?
answer_data: citation origin mode: direct or inherited
reference to the intermediate document where inherited
agent that recorded the citation and the time it was recorded

data_elements.name: Evidence reference

finding.inline_only_rationale: A citation binding must remain a reference, a type code, a locator and a stance. Locators are held inline precisely so that resolution always goes back to the governed evidence item.

composition.purpose: Register the decision under its knowledge parent. Generic assertion identity, truth-value, endorsement and claim-conflict machinery stay with the parent; this model adds only decision-specific specialisation, namely the alternative set, criteria, evaluation and disposition.

Bind evidence cited in support of an evaluation result or a declared assumption, carrying the evidence identifier and the role of the citation. Evidence appraisal, sufficiency, integrity and chain of custody remain with the target and are never reproduced here.

Reference the activity that produced and approved the decision, so that participants, deliberation, quorum and approval execution can be resolved. This model carries the reference and any decision-specific binding parameters only; the activity's lifecycle and execution semantics stay with the target.

Reference the record that expresses, files or publishes this decision content, following the Work and Expression separation from Manifestation and Item. Rendering, formatting, publication, preservation and record-level retention execution stay with the target.

Where the decision is judicial, align the outcome content to the judgment's decision section and its background and motivation structure. The judgment's binding legal force, enforceability and citation regime remain with the target; alignment asserts no conformance.

Carry the back-reference from a decision to the change request it resolves, matching the incoming relation in the ledger. The request's own lifecycle, prioritisation and the implementation, monitoring and compliance work that follows the decision belong to the target.

composition.target: OMG Decision Model and Notation (DMN) version 1.5
composition.purpose: Align framing vocabulary to DMN element names for interchange: question, allowedAnswers, informationRequirement, knowledgeRequirement, supportedObjective, impactedPerformanceIndicator and decision table hitPolicy. Alignment only; no conformance is claimed, DMN identifiers are document-scoped and do not satisfy the identity priority, and execution of DMN decision logic stays with a decision service.

composition.target: Jurisdictional appraisal and record-of-decision profiles (HM Treasury Green Book, US NEPA record-of-decision pattern)
composition.purpose: Bind an optional jurisdictional profile that adds required content elements, such as a mandatory business-as-usual baseline, recorded reasons for eliminating alternatives, identification of a preferable alternative and declared mitigation conditions. Profiles are opt-in per decision type; none is a global default and the NEPA pattern is cited as historical.

Registry-declared parent. Decision rationale is a specialisation of governed assertion content: premises and conclusions are references to claims that WM-KNW-007 identifies, versions and verifies. This model adds only the argument role a claim occupies, the version pinned at reasoning time and any marked local restatement; it never issues claim identity, changes claim wording or records claim verification status.

Decision rationale cites evidence. This model carries the evidence reference, the citation type, the locator into the cited resource, the citation stance and the decision-local appraisal of how far the evidence bears on this decision. Evidence identity, acquisition, chain of custody, intrinsic certainty grading and evidence retention remain in WM-KNW-008 and are carried by reference; a referenced certainty grade is read and reproduced unchanged with its read time, never recomputed here.

Incoming registry-declared relation: a change request is resolved by a decision and references the decision record. This model exposes stable rationale identifiers so that such a reference can resolve, and nothing more. Change-request intake, triage, workflow and closure are owned by WM-ACT-032, and no function here advances or evaluates a change request.

composition.target: OMG Structured Assurance Case Metamodel (SACM) 2.3, Argumentation package
composition.purpose: Alignment target for argument structure: claims, argument reasoning, asserted inference, asserted evidence and counter-argument or counter-evidence links. Mapping is asserted at the level of element roles only; no conformance is claimed and the alignment does not import SACM's assurance-case lifecycle or its notation.

Alignment target for representing inference, conflict and preference as first-class nodes and for scheme forms carrying premises, conclusions, exceptions and presumptions. Used to justify first-class inference elements and scheme references; AIF's dialogue extensions are outside this model's scope.

model.name: Decision / Approval Record
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to identify, create, interpret, validate and operate an authoritative record of a decision or approval: what was decided, on what question, by whom under what authority, on what reasons and evidence, with what conditions, from when until when it is valid, and how it is superseded, challenged, disclosed and retained.
model.scope_statement: The model covers the record that constitutes or evidences a discrete decision or approval act and the act's decision-relevant attributes. It treats the decision act and the record of it as distinct but co-modelled: the act supplies authority, outcome, reasons and timing; the record supplies identity, versioned expression, integrity evidence, disclosure and disposition. It spans administrative decisions, judicial judgments, corporate and board resolutions, delegated sign-offs, gate/change approvals and retained machine authorization decisions. It excludes the deliberative occasion, the containing case or procedure, the norms applied, party master data and generic record custody mechanics, which belong to sibling or parent models.
in_scope: Decision identity, versioned expression identity and classification of decision or approval type
Decided question, outcome/disposition, attached conditions, obligations and advice
Statement of reasons, alternatives considered and rejected, evidence and findings of fact relied on
Decision authority, legal or constitutional basis, delegation, approval limits, quorum and voting
Approval participation acts, dissent, abstention, recusal and conflict-of-interest declarations
Attestation evidence: signature, seal, trusted time-stamp token, hash and finality of the record
Distinct decision-relevant times: taken, consented, issued, served, published, in force, recorded
Validity window, retroactivity, conditions of validity, expiry and renewal
Status model, finality, supersession, amendment, corrigendum, revocation and annulment
Challenge, appeal, review outcome and suspensive effect
Automated, assisted and solely automated decision modes with human oversight and contestability
Publication, individual notification/service, access classification, redaction and anonymisation
Decision-specific retention triggers, disposition and disposal/legal hold
Alignment to external decision identifiers and vocabularies (ECLI, Akoma Ntoso, PROV, DCMI, XACML)
out_of_scope: The deliberative occasion itself — agenda, attendance, minutes as a whole (WM-ACT-025 Meeting)
The containing administrative case, application or procedure lifecycle (WM-POL-017)
Generic record custody, storage media, format migration and preservation mechanics (parent WM-REC-001)
The normative content of the policy, statute, rule or standard being applied (policy/rule sibling model)
Master data for persons, organisational units and positions holding decision roles (party/agent sibling model)
Authoring and administration of machine access-control policies; only a retained decision result is in scope
Contract or agreement terms that a decision may authorise (agreement sibling model)
Workflow engine internals, task queues and routing logic that carry an approval request
Downstream financial posting, permit issuance or benefit payment produced by a decision

boundary_notes.distinction: A meeting is an occasion; a decision record is an outcome assertion. The relationship is optional in both directions: Delaware General Corporation Law §141(f) permits board action without any meeting by unanimous written or electronic consent, and delegated single-signature approvals never involve a meeting. Meeting attendance and agenda stay in the meeting model; only the linkage, the agenda item decided and the quorum/vote result attach to the decision record.

A case is the procedural container and may hold many decisions — procedural, interim, partial and final. Case state transitions are driven by decisions but are not decisions. Ex parte communications belong to the case record and are referenced by the decision record only where a rule requires them to be placed on the record of decision.

The parent supplies generic record properties: authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability as record characteristics, custody, format and preservation. WM-REC-010 adds only what is decision-specific — authority, outcome, reasons, validity and supersession — and must not restate parent mechanics.

A PDP result has the same logical shape (decision value, status, obligations, advice, applicable policy identifiers) but is normally ephemeral and produced at log scale. The boundary is retention as a record: a PDP result becomes an instance of this model only when it is captured and managed as a record. XACML decision values are an alignment vocabulary, not the canonical outcome set.

A judgment is a specialised decision record with a governed global identifier (ECLI) and a document structure of introduction, background, motivation and decision. That structure is judicial and must not be imposed on administrative or corporate decisions; court organisation, procedure and case-law citation networks are out of scope.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Electronic signature, seal and time-stamp evidence
boundary_notes.distinction: Attestation evidence is referenced, not owned. The decision record holds pointers to signature/seal objects and time-stamp tokens plus a verification verdict and verification time; the cryptographic object model, trust lists and long-term validation data belong to a signature-evidence sibling model.

Boundary under review. In this model an approval is either an outcome value of a decision or a participation act within one, because the cited sources give approvals no independent identity. Standing authorisations such as licences and permits do have independent validity and holders, and may justify a separate sibling model; flagged rather than assumed.

ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 treats an architecture decision as pertaining to concerns and affecting architecture description elements, with rationale covering alternatives not chosen. That is a design-governance specialisation of the same shape; the architecture description, viewpoints and models it affects are out of scope here.

composition.purpose: WM-REC-010 is a specialisation of the generic record. The parent owns record characteristics, custody, format, preservation and baseline metadata; this model adds only decision-specific authority, outcome, reasons, validity and supersession semantics and must not restate parent mechanics.

A meeting may produce decision records. The link is optional in both directions because Delaware §141(f) unanimous written consent and delegated sign-offs produce decisions with no meeting at all. Attendance, agenda and full minutes stay in the meeting model; only the occasion reference, agenda item and quorum/vote result attach here.

An administrative case ends or changes state through decisions. The case model owns the procedure and its state; this model owns each decision within it. One case may compose many decisions of different procedural stages, and one decision may close or alter several cases.

composition.target: Party / agent master-data model (sibling candidate, model ID not yet registered)
composition.purpose: Deciders, approvers, dissenters, addressees and affected parties must resolve to governed party identifiers rather than being named inline, so that authority, delegation and conflicts can be verified against master data.

composition.target: Policy, rule and mandate model (sibling candidate, model ID not yet registered)
composition.purpose: The authority basis, the rules applied and the machine policy sets evaluated are cited at a specific in-force version. Their normative content belongs to the policy model; this model records only which version was relied upon and to what effect.

composition.target: Electronic signature, seal and time-stamp evidence model (sibling candidate, model ID not yet registered)
composition.purpose: Attestation evidence is mixed in rather than owned: this model holds references, coverage statements and verification verdicts, while the cryptographic object model, trust anchors and long-term validation material live in the evidence model.

composition.target: Retention schedule and disposition authority model (sibling candidate, model ID not yet registered)
composition.purpose: Retention periods, disposition outcomes and appraisal criteria are jurisdiction-specific and change independently of decisions. This model references a schedule item and records the resolved trigger, never embedding a period.

Alignment only. The decision act maps to prov:Activity, deciders and systems to prov:Agent, the record to prov:Entity, roles to a qualified prov:Association with prov:hadRole, delegation to prov:actedOnBehalfOf, supersession to prov:wasDerivedFrom and cessation of effect to prov:wasInvalidatedBy. PROV has no native concept of competence, quorum or validity window, so the alignment is partial.

Alignment only, for retained machine authorization decisions: Decision, Status, Obligations, AssociatedAdvice and PolicyIdentifierList map onto outcome, status detail, obligations, advisory items and applied policy identifiers. Permit/Deny must not be equated with a reasoned grant or refusal, and NotApplicable has no administrative equivalent.

composition.target: ECLI (European Case Law Identifier) and OASIS Akoma Ntoso v1.0
composition.purpose: Alignment for judicial and legislative decisions: ECLI supplies a governed global identifier for the decision as a work; Akoma Ntoso supplies the Work/Expression/Manifestation/Item identity levels and the judgment structure. Neither is imposed on administrative or corporate decisions.

Alignment for the temporal and supersession vocabulary: valid, issued, created, modified, dateAccepted, replaces, isReplacedBy, provenance, accessRights and conformsTo. Adopted because these terms keep validity, issuance and modification separate, which a single decision date collapses.

Alignment for design-governance decisions, where a decision pertains to concerns, affects description elements and carries rationale covering alternatives not chosen. Used to justify the options-considered and reasons findings as a general pattern, not to import architecture description structure.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently converge on entry_kind=entity for a single authoritative decision or approval instance, and both exclude the same neighbours (the meeting/occasion WM-ACT-025, the administrative case WM-POL-017, parent record mechanics WM-REC-001, and party/policy master data). The base draws the sharper internal line: the decision act supplies authority, outcome, reasons and timing while the record supplies identity, versioned expression, integrity evidence, disclosure and disposition, co-modelled but distinct. Approval is accepted as an outcome value or a participation act rather than an independent object, because neither source set gives approval acts independent identity. Two carve-outs are recorded rather than resolved: standing authorisations (licences, permits) with independent holders and validity may warrant a sibling model, and reusable executable decision logic (OMG DMN) is confirmed out of scope as a sibling. Neither carve-out changes the entry kind or blocks a research draft.

decisions.concept: Base selection: Claude as structural base
decisions.rationale: Clearest complete boundaries, not size: eight boundary notes each with a stated distinction and source refs, an explicit act-versus-record separation, a nine-item out-of-scope list, and adversarial checks that actually tested the boundary (approval as a sibling model, duplication against the parent record model, rejection of a single decision_date). Grok's boundary work is sound but leans on tier-3 ADR practice for structural vocabulary and lacks the identity/expression and disclosure depth.

decisions.concept: Decision act and record of the act co-modelled but distinct
decisions.rationale: Both providers need the separation and only the base states it operationally: the act supplies authority, outcome, reasons and timing; the record supplies identity, versioned expression, integrity evidence, disclosure and disposition. This also settles the identifier question (which of the two an identifier designates) that both packs raise.

decisions.concept: Approval as an independent object with its own identity
decisions.rationale: Neither source set gives approval acts independent identity, so approval stays an outcome value or a participation act. Standing authorisations such as licences and permits do have independent holders and validity windows and may need a sibling model; this remains an open boundary flagged in the draft, not something resolved by assertion.

decisions.concept: OMG DMN boundary: reusable executable decision logic versus an instance record
decisions.disposition: accepted as a boundary note only, no node added
decisions.rationale: Grok's DMN distinction is the one boundary the base is missing, and it prevents a real failure mode where decision tables and FEEL logic get modelled as approval records, hiding the approver and validity surface. It belongs in boundary_notes with grok SRC-004 as the reference; it does not justify a finding, because base f03 q03-family already classifies the instance.

decisions.concept: ISO 23081 authenticity, integrity, reliability and usability as a finding here
decisions.rationale: The base explicitly assigns generic record characteristics, custody, format and preservation to parent WM-REC-001 and adds only decision-specific semantics. Importing Grok's authenticity-integrity finding would restate parent mechanics and create two owners for fixity. Decision-specific attestation stays with f15 (signature, seal, time-stamp, digest, verification verdict).

decisions.concept: ADR status vocabulary (proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated, superseded) as canonical
decisions.disposition: rejected as canonical; retained as an alignment
decisions.rationale: Grok itself notes these originate in software-engineering practice and are not legal status codes; they cannot express finality, annulment, stay or suspensive effect. The base's governed enumeration with a transition table and an explicit terminal-state question is more general and covers the ADR set as a profile.

decisions.concept: MADR decision drivers and recorded consequences
decisions.rationale: Drivers duplicate base f05 q05-concerns (stakeholder concerns, requirements and criteria the decision had to address) and f09 q09-criteria (criteria and weights fixed before assessment). Recorded consequences rest only on tier-3 practice sources and partly overlap f07 obligations and f21 relations to later decisions. Duplicate structure on weak support is worse than the gap.

decisions.concept: Ex parte start-of-ban timing and oral-then-memorialised capture gap
decisions.disposition: rejected as findings; flagged for question-level enrichment
decisions.rationale: Both are genuine primary-sourced details (§557(d) designation of when the prohibition begins; capture completeness where a decision is given orally and memorialised later) but the enclosing Grok findings duplicate base f14, f10 q10-exparte and f18 q18-draft-boundary. They should be added as questions under those findings during draft editing rather than as competing nodes.

decisions.concept: Grok approvers-and-roles (consulted/informed roles, non-human decider accountability)
decisions.rationale: Base q11-who already separates the decider from anyone who prepared, recommended or merely signed, and f23/f24 handle system attribution and residual human responsibility with stronger evidence (WP29 guidance, AI Act, XACML). The consulted/informed split is tier-3 RACI practice and adds no decision-relevant constraint.

decisions.concept: XACML four-valued outcome vocabulary as the canonical outcome set
decisions.disposition: rejected; retained as a declared-lossy alignment
decisions.rationale: Reaffirming the base's own adversarial finding: Permit/Deny/NotApplicable/Indeterminate cannot express grant-with-conditions, partial grant, deferral or withdrawal, and NotApplicable has no administrative meaning. The mapping stays recorded with its loss so a consumer is not misled.

decisions.concept: Retention trigger as an explicit choice rather than record creation
decisions.rationale: Anchoring retention to creation would destroy long-validity decisions such as permits while still in force. The base models the trigger as a choice among creation, issuance, expiry of validity, exhaustion of challenge routes and case closure, and stores the resolved trigger timestamp; Grok's retention finding is compatible and adds nothing beyond it.

decisions.concept: Access-event auditing and the wider security dimension
decisions.rationale: The base marks security as a gap (key management, trust anchors, cryptographic agility, long-term validation data), and Grok's only access-audit question (reads, exports, failed attempts) carries no primary requirement source in either pack. Adding a node now would assert a control neither provider evidenced; it is recorded as deferred research instead.

decisions.concept: Citation of record for 5 U.S.C. §557
decisions.rationale: Grok cites a NARA-hosted APA page last reviewed 2016-08-15; the base cites govinfo United States Code, 2023 edition. The imported §557-derived nodes (f30, f31) must carry the govinfo 2023 citation, with the NARA page demoted to a corroborating link, so no imported node rests on a stale reproduction.

decisions.concept: Machine authorization results as instances of this model
decisions.disposition: accepted from base with the retention test
decisions.rationale: A PDP result shares the logical shape but is ephemeral and produced at log scale. The base's rule — it becomes an instance only when captured and managed as a record — is the only workable boundary and keeps f23/f24 from swallowing runtime telemetry.

publicationHolds: Source and live-version verification is incomplete and remains a hold. Every accepted source URL, version pin and issuing-body status must be re-resolved live before publication, including the two Grok-derived citations imported with f29 and f32 (DCMI Terms 2020-01-20, PROV-DM W3C Recommendation 30 April 2013).

Paywalled and unretrievable normative text: ISO 15489-1:2016, ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 and the ISO 23081 series were never read at clause level (iso.org returned HTTP 403 to both providers), so all claims attributed to them are catalogue, abstract or secondary-summary level. No conformance statement may be published until re-verified against purchased copies.

EUR-Lex was not retrievable in either research run. GDPR Article 22 was consulted only through an unofficial reproduction (tier 3), the AI Act only through a Commission overview page, and eIDAS Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 not at all. The automation bundle (f23, f24) may be published as a research draft but no article-level obligation, signature-assurance tier or seal semantics may be asserted.

Multi-profile domain validation is incomplete and remains a hold. The model has been exercised against US federal formal adjudication, Delaware corporate action, EU judicial identification, ADR practice and machine authorization only. It must be stress-tested against at least one sector approval regime (medicines or device authorisation, building or environmental permitting, credit underwriting, research ethics) and at least one non-EU/US legal tradition before any publication beyond a research draft.

The two imported §557-derived nodes (f30-adjudicative-grade-and-conclusiveness, f31-completeness-of-rulings-and-implementation-confirmation) must be published as US formal-adjudication conditional, never as default grades or default completeness duties, and must carry the govinfo 2023 United States Code citation rather than the NARA reproduction.
deferredResearch: Standing authorisations (licences, permits, accreditations) with independent holders, renewal cycles and their own validity: determine whether these require a sibling model or can remain outcome values of this one. This is the base's own flagged open boundary and the single largest structural risk in the model.

Voting and consent mechanics beyond quorum-and-simple-majority: weighted voting, qualified majority with population thresholds, consensus and objection-based procedures, ranked and multi-round ballots, and proxy or alternate voting are representable but not individually modelled by either provider.

Security dimension: key management, trust-anchor governance, cryptographic agility, long-term validation material for archival attestation, and access-event auditing (reads, exports, failed attempts). The base marks security as a gap and Grok's single access-audit question has no primary requirement source.

Multilingual authentic-text divergence: no rule exists in either pack for resolving substantive conflict between equally authentic language versions; expression identity alone does not settle which text governs.

Non-Western, customary and consensus-based decision traditions, and non-adversarial procedures, were researched by neither provider. The model's quorum-and-majority orientation may be a poor fit and should be tested before the coverage claim is widened.

Question-level enrichment carried forward from rejected Grok nodes: the §557(d) designation of when ex parte prohibitions begin (under f10 or f14), and the oral-then-memorialised capture-completeness exception (under f18 q18-draft-boundary).

model.name: Claim / Proposition
model.purpose: Provide a format-neutral record of a truth-apt assertion: what proposition is asserted, under what scope and qualification, by whom and with what standing, how it relates to other claims, which evidence and assessments it references, and how the claim record itself is identified, versioned, validated, restricted and disposed of. The model records assertion, not verdicts.
model.scope_statement: WM-KNW-007 covers the claim record as an object of knowledge management: propositional content and canonical form, identity and equivalence, scope and qualification (subject, place, time, conditions, measurand), stated calibrated uncertainty, the assertion act and asserting authority, provenance and ownership of the record, typed claim-to-claim relations, bound references to evidence and assessments, record lifecycle and versioning, well-formedness validation, sensitivity/access classification and disposition, and interoperability projections. It excludes the evidence items themselves, the appraisal of evidence bodies, the application and evaluation of inference schemes, the execution of fact-checking or verification, policy enforcement, and runtime audit trails owned by other systems.
in_scope: Canonical truth-apt statement, its language, atomicity and optional normalized subject-property-value or logical form
Claim identity, aliases, equivalence, restatement and translation relationships
Scope qualifiers: subject or population range, spatial extent, validity interval, conditions, assumptions, scenarios and known defeaters
Quantitative content of measurement claims: measurand, value, unit, stated coverage interval
Calibrated qualification stated on the claim: confidence and likelihood terms, scale reference and traceable-account pointer
The assertion act: claimant, role, illocutionary commitment, first and subsequent appearances, asserting authority and mandate
Provenance, attribution, derivation, ownership, stewardship and rights of the claim record
Typed claim-to-claim relations: entailment, specialization, contradiction, rebuttal, preference, supersession
Bound references to evidence items, external assessments/reviews and argument structures, carrying binding parameters only
Record lifecycle states, transitions, versioning, patch rules and externally issued retraction or correction references
Well-formedness shapes, required-field profiles and quality/testability signals for the record
Sensitivity classification, access policy expression, retention schedule, tombstones and disposition rules
Interoperability alignments and lossy-projection declarations across PROV-O, schema.org, VC 2.0, AIF, nanopublication and RDF 1.2
out_of_scope: Evidence items, citations, source descriptions, evidence typology, evidence appraisal and evidence lifecycle, which are owned by WM-KNW-008
Application and evaluation of inference, conflict and preference rules (AIF RA, CA and PA node semantics) and any defeasible-reasoning engine
Execution of fact-checking, verification or adjudication workflows, and the rating semantics, reviewer processes and audit trails of assessment systems
Runtime enforcement or evaluation of access and usage policies, and policy-decision logging
The real-world entities, events and quantities the claim is about, which belong to subject-domain models
Documents, publications and media that carry a claim, and publisher retraction workflows executed under NISO CREC
Cryptographic proof, credential status lists and verification procedures of Verifiable Credentials transport
Agent belief state, trust scoring of claimants or sources, and reputation computation
Storage engines, serializations and access interfaces (JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MCP, MongoDB are projections)
Generic knowledge-asset register mechanics inherited from the parent model WM-KNW-001

boundary_notes.distinction: This model carries the evidence reference, the binding role (supports, challenges, qualifies), directionality and a locally stated binding weight. It never carries the evidence item's description, provenance, appraisal grade or lifecycle; those are dereferenced from WM-KNW-008 and are never copied into a claim record.

A claim corresponds to the AIF I-node level. Applications of rules of inference (RA), conflict (CA) and preference (PA), argument-scheme definitions and any evaluation of argument acceptability belong to an argumentation model. This model records only that a claim occupies a premise or conclusion role in an externally identified argument structure.

This model holds the reviewable claim and a reference to reviews of it. The review's rating scale, reviewer identity workflow, publication and audit trail are owned by the reviewing system; a review reference is never read as a truth value on the claim record.

PROV terms are used as alignment for attribution, derivation, revision and invalidation of the claim record. This model does not own generic Activity/Agent modelling, provenance-of-provenance bundles or provenance query semantics.

A VC claim is a subject-property-value assertion carried inside a credential secured by proof. This model treats the proposition independently of transport: credential validity, status and cryptographic verification are owned by credential models and must not be interpreted as claim truth or claim lifecycle.

A quantitative claim references a measurand, a value with unit and a stated coverage interval. The measurement procedure, instrument, calibration and metrological traceability chain belong to a measurement or observation model.

This model expresses sensitivity classes and ODRL policies about claim records. ODRL is a policy expression language that defines no enforcement or evaluation semantics, and none is claimed here; decisioning and its logs belong to the adopting Dimension's platform.

Generic knowledge-asset identity, register governance, stewardship and licensing are inherited through the CHILD link. This model specializes only what makes a record truth-apt: proposition, qualification, assertion and claim relations.

bundle.name: Proposition Content and Identity
bundle.description: What proposition the record asserts, in what form, of what kind, and how that proposition is identified and recognised as the same claim across restatements, translations and systems.

layer.name: Content and Form

finding.name: Canonical Statement

Which normalized structured form represents the statement for machine comparison?

questions.text: Does the statement bundle several separately assertable propositions that must be split into distinct records?
answer_data: Split or retain decision with rationale

questions.text: Is the canonical text a verbatim quotation of the claimant or a curator paraphrase, and in which language?
answer_data: Locator of the quoted passage if verbatim

data_elements.name: Canonical statement text
data_elements.description: The declarative sentence asserted by this record, stored exactly as curated.

data_elements.name: Statement language tag

data_elements.name: Normalized statement form
data_elements.description: Structured subject-property-value or logical rendering of the statement used for comparison and projection.

data_elements.name: Atomicity verdict

finding.inline_only_rationale: The canonical statement and its normalized form are the record's own primary field values, not a separately managed deliverable; the nanopublication guidance to keep assertions minimal implies inline triples rather than a document, and treating the statement as an artifact would create a second identity for the same proposition.

Which governed global identifier or IRI resolves to this claim record and stays resolvable for its retention period?

data_elements.name: Canonical content digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical normalized statement, used only as a secondary equivalence key.

artifacts.name: Claim Identifier Register
artifacts.description: Register binding primary identifiers to claim records and to alias identifiers, recording the issuing authority, the identity-priority tier applied and the resolution commitment for each namespace.

bundle.description: The conditions under which the claim is asserted to hold: over what subjects, where, when, under what assumptions, with what measured content, and with what calibrated confidence the asserter attached to it.

layer.name: Scope Qualifiers
layer.description: Subject range, spatial and temporal extent, and the conditions, assumptions and known defeaters that bound the assertion.

finding.name: Subject and Population Scope
finding.description: The entities the claim ranges over: the named subject or the population definition with inclusion and exclusion criteria, and the level of aggregation at which the claim is asserted.

questions.text: Which entity or population is the claim about, identified rather than merely named in prose?
answer_data: Subject reference to a domain identifier
Fallback description where no identifier exists

questions.text: Which inclusion and exclusion criteria delimit the population, and what is explicitly outside it?
At which level of aggregation does the claim hold: individual, group, cohort or population average?
answer_data: Warning where the claim may be read as an individual-level assertion

questions.text: Does the claim name an identifiable natural person, and does that trigger sensitivity classification?

data_elements.name: Population definition

data_elements.name: Aggregation level

Publishing them as an artifact would either duplicate the domain model's entity descriptions or create a parallel population registry this model has no mandate to own.

bundle.description: The conditions under which the claim is asserted to hold: over what subjects, where, when, under what assumptions, with what measured content, and with what calibrated confidence the asserter attached to it.

layer.description: Subject range, spatial and temporal extent, and the conditions, assumptions and known defeaters that bound the assertion.

finding.name: Conditions, Assumptions and Known Defeaters
finding.description: The scenario, background assumptions, ceteris paribus conditions and explicitly acknowledged defeating circumstances under which the claim is or is not asserted to hold.

questions.text: Under which scenario, model or set of background assumptions is the claim asserted?
Which circumstances, if they obtained, would defeat the claim without falsifying it outright?
Which conditions are load-bearing such that changing them creates a different claim rather than a variant?
Are any assumptions implicit in the wording and not yet stated in structured fields?

data_elements.description: Identifier of the scenario, pathway or model under which the claim is asserted.

data_elements.description: A background condition the claim depends on, stated explicitly.

data_elements.name: Known defeater
data_elements.description: An acknowledged circumstance that would defeat the claim, with its defeater type.

Recording a defeater is a note that a defeating circumstance is acknowledged; evaluating whether it actually defeats the claim belongs to an argumentation model, so no local artifact should imply that adjudication happened here.

layer.description: The act of asserting: claimant, commitment, appearance context, and whether the claimant held authority to assert.

finding.name: Claimant and Assertion Act
finding.description: Who asserted the proposition, in what capacity and with what degree of commitment, together with the first and subsequent contexts in which the assertion appeared.

questions.text: Which agent asserted this proposition, identified rather than described by name alone?
In what capacity did the claimant assert it: personally, on behalf of an organisation, or as a reported position?
answer_data: Reporting chain where the assertion is second-hand

questions.text: How strong was the commitment: asserted outright, hypothesised, attributed to others, or quoted without endorsement?
answer_data: Wording that signals the commitment level

questions.text: Where did the claim first appear and where else has it appeared since?
answer_data: Medium and audience for each appearance

data_elements.description: Identifier of the agent that asserted the proposition.

data_elements.name: Assertion capacity
data_elements.description: The capacity in which the claimant asserted, including representation of an organisation.

data_elements.name: Commitment level
data_elements.description: Degree of assertive commitment, from outright assertion to unendorsed quotation.

data_elements.name: Appearance locator

finding.inline_only_rationale: The assertion act is captured as references to agents and to appearance locations in documents owned by content and publication models. finding.name: Conflict and Contradiction
finding.description: Registration that two claims stand in conflict, with the conflict type and the point of disagreement recorded, and with resolution explicitly not performed here.

questions.text: Which claims contradict this one, and is the conflict rebutting the content or undercutting its support?
Is the apparent conflict genuine, or does it dissolve once scope qualifiers are compared?
Who registered the conflict and when, and what status does registration confer on either claim?
answer_data: Status effect declared by the owning package

questions.text: Which system, outside this model, is responsible for resolving or adjudicating the conflict?
answer_data: Expected form of the resolution output

data_elements.name: Conflict edge
data_elements.description: Qualified edge registering conflict with another claim, with conflict type and disagreement point.

data_elements.name: Conflict registration event
data_elements.description: Who registered the conflict and when, in RFC 3339 with offset.

data_elements.name: Resolution referral
data_elements.description: Reference to the external body or system responsible for adjudicating the conflict.

finding.inline_only_rationale: Conflicts are registered as qualified edges plus a registration event. A conflict register artifact would read as an adjudication docket and would encroach on the argumentation model that owns conflict-rule application and on the assessment systems that issue verdicts.

layer.description: Recorded relations between claim records: entailment and specialization, conflict, and preference or supersession, registered without being adjudicated.

finding.name: Preference and Supersession
finding.description: Recorded orderings between claims: an asserted preference between competing claims, and the supersession chain by which a later claim replaces an earlier one.

questions.text: Which competing claim is preferred over which, and by whose criterion?
answer_data: Asserting agent and date of the preference

questions.text: Which claim does this one supersede, and which claim supersedes it?
Does supersession change the earlier claim's status, or leave it valid for its original period?
How are supersession chains kept acyclic and traversable to the current claim?

data_elements.name: Preference edge
data_elements.description: Qualified edge asserting preference between two competing claims, with criterion and asserter.

data_elements.name: Supersedes reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the claim this record supersedes.

data_elements.name: Superseded-by reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the claim that supersedes this record.

finding.inline_only_rationale: Preference and supersession are directional edges evaluated at query time to find the current claim. Materialising a chain artifact would freeze a view that must stay derivable from the edges, and preference application in argument evaluation is owned by the argumentation model.

In what role does each bound item stand: supporting, challenging, qualifying or merely cited?
answer_data: Curator note on the role assignment

questions.text: What weight or relevance does this claim's curator attach to the binding, and how is that distinguished from the evidence's own appraisal?

How does the claim map to the AIF I-node level, and which node types are deliberately not represented here?
answer_data: Excluded node types (RA, CA, PA, F)
